name: Nem cho huyen
summary: Fermented pork from Tuy Phước, chewy, nubbly, sour, and crisp with a clean sweetness. It is less soft than nem Thủ Đức and less sweet than nem Lai Vung or nem An Cựu.
origin: Huyện Tuy Phước. An old verse places it at Vĩnh Thạnh.
texture: A bite is chewy, nubbly, sour, and crisp, with a clean sweetness.
howToEat: Peel the two banana-leaf wraps and the guava leaf. Eat it fresh, or grilled over charcoal, with coriander, perilla, rau răm, banana, star fruit, cucumber, garlic, and chili, and fish sauce or soy.
It also comes as a rice-paper roll called bánh cuốn: a skewer of nem, herbs, and a few fried chả ram. The sauce decides the roll.
seoTitle: Nem cho huyen — Tuy Phuoc pork
seoDescription: Nem chợ huyện is Tuy Phước fermented pork, chewy, sour, and crisp, eaten fresh or grilled with herbs, or rolled in rice paper.
